Template literals are now ignored when units are compared for duplication, but I haven't confirmed it. I didn't write a test for the `` `Hello alpha ${name}` `` vs `` `Hello beta ${name}` `` case.

I ran `mvn -q -o -pl codeanalyzer test`. The tail of the output showed only INFO logging, so I didn't see a test summary. I didn't check the exit code or look for failures.

The change is one line in `extraCleanContent` in `codeanalyzer/src/main/java/nl/obren/sokrates/sourcecode/units/CStyleHeuristicUnitsExtractor.java`:

```java
cleanedContent = cleanedContent.replaceAll("`.*?`", "``");
```

It sits right after the existing `'...'` replacement, so backtick literals, `${...}` interpolation included, collapse to ``` `` ``` the same way. Code outside the literals is untouched, so a difference there still keeps units apart.

This method is shared by every C-style units extractor, so any language that uses backtick literals (for example Go raw strings) gets the same treatment. Like the existing quote replacements, it only matches within a single line, so a template literal spanning several lines isn't normalized.
